subject.title: feat(codex): surface native questions and goals

question: Should OpenClaw universally disable Codex native goal continuation for managed threads, or preserve an explicit existing `features.goals: true` opt-in while using a safer default for otherwise unconfigured threads?
rationale: The branch deliberately changes an existing upstream feature setting to prevent autonomous turns, but that safety policy can break explicitly configured goal-enabled workflows; code inspection cannot choose the permanent compatibility contract.

options.title: Preserve explicit opt-ins
options.body: Use the safe OpenClaw default only when `features.goals` is absent, while retaining an explicit user-provided value and documenting the continuation implications.

options.title: Force goals off
options.body: Always set `features.goals` to false and explicitly accept, document, and prove the upgrade break for previously goal-enabled threads.

options.title: Split goal control out
options.body: Land structured questions separately and defer native goal commands and continuation policy to a dedicated follow-up decision.

recommendation.title: Preserve explicit opt-ins
recommendation.body: Use the safe OpenClaw default only when `features.goals` is absent, while retaining an explicit user-provided value and documenting the continuation implications.
